requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getcall` operation IS used to accept calls.
requirements.original: The getcall operation is used to accept calls.

requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getcall` operation has the syntax [`@nodefault`] (ObjectReference | `any port` | `any from` PortArrayRef) "." `getcall` ["(" TemplateInstance ")"] [`from` Address] ["->" [`param` "(" parameter assignment list ")"] [`sender` ValueRef] [`@index value` ValueRef]], where a parameter assignment is either a list of "ValueRef := [@decoded [(Expression)]] ParameterIdentifier" items or a positional list of ValueRef or "-" items.
requirements.original:
[ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any port | any from PortArrayRef ) "." getcall
  [ "(" TemplateInstance ")" ] 
  [ from Address ]
  [ "->" [ param "(" { ( ValueRef":=" [ @decoded [ "(" Expression ")" ] ] 
          ParameterIdentifier ) "," } |
          { ( ValueRef| "-" ) "," } 
         ")" ]
     [ sender ValueRef] 
     [ @index value ValueRef] ]

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: The Address in the `from` clause of a `getcall` operation CAN be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRefs or `any component`.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "any component"._

requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getcall` operation specifies that a test component accepts a call from the SUT or from another test component.
requirements.original: The getcall operation is used to specify that a test component accepts a call from the SUT, or another test component.

requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.condition: the matching criteria associated to the getcall operation are fulfilled
requirements.canonical: If the matching criteria of a `getcall` operation are fulfilled, the `getcall` operation SHALL remove the top call from the incoming port queue.
requirements.original: The getcall operation shall remove the top call from the incoming port queue, if, and only if, the matching criteria associated to the getcall operation are fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.condition: the matching criteria associated to the getcall operation are not fulfilled
requirements.canonical: If the matching criteria of a `getcall` operation are not fulfilled, the `getcall` operation SHALL NOT remove the top call from the incoming port queue.
requirements.original: The getcall operation shall remove the top call from the incoming port queue, if, and only if, the matching criteria associated to the getcall operation are fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-criteria
requirements.canonical: The matching criteria of a `getcall` operation relate to the signature of the call to be processed and to the communication partner.
requirements.original: These matching criteria are related to the signature of the call to be processed and the communication partner.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-criteria
requirements.canonical: The matching criteria for the signature of a `getcall` operation MAY be specified in-line or be derived from a signature template.
requirements.original: The matching criteria for the signature may either be specified in-line or be derived from a signature template.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-part
requirements.canonical: The assignment of `in` and `inout` parameter values to variables SHALL be made in the assignment part of the `getcall` operation.
requirements.original: The assignment of in and inout parameter values to variables shall be made in the assignment part of the getcall operation.

requirements.subject: ent:signature-template
requirements.canonical: Keeping parameter assignment in the assignment part allows signature templates to be used in `getcall` operations in the same manner as templates are used for types.
requirements.original: This allows the use of signature templates in getcall operations in the same manner as templates are used for types.

requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.condition: one-to-many connection
requirements.canonical: In case of one-to-many connections, a `getcall` operation MAY be restricted to a certain communication partner.
requirements.original: A getcall operation may be restricted to a certain communication partner in case of one-to-many connections.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: The restriction of a `getcall` operation to a communication partner SHALL be denoted by the `from` keyword followed by an address or component reference, a list of address or component references, or `any component`.
requirements.original: This restriction shall be denoted by using the from keyword followed by a specification of an address or component reference, a list of address or component references or any component.

requirements.subject: ent:one-to-one-connection
requirements.canonical: A one-to-one connection IS a simple case of a one-to-many connection, and a `getcall` operation on a one-to-one connection MAY use the `from` clause.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The one-to-one connection is considered to be a simple case of the one-to-many connections and allows the usage of the from-clause.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-part
requirements.canonical: The optional assignment part of the `getcall` operation comprises the assignment of `in` and `inout` parameter values to variables and the retrieval of the address of the calling component.
requirements.original: The (optional) assignment part of the getcall operation comprises the assignment of in and inout parameter values to variables and the retrieval of the address of the calling component.

requirements.subject: ent:param-clause
requirements.canonical: The `param` keyword IS used to retrieve the parameter values of a call accepted by a `getcall` operation.
requirements.original: The keyword param is used to retrieve the parameter values of a call.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: When assigning individual parameters of a call in a `getcall` operation, encoded parameters MAY be decoded prior to assignment using the `@decoded` modifier.
requirements.original: When assigning individual parameters of a call, encoded parameters can be decoded prior to assignment using the @decoded modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the @decoded modifier is used
requirements.canonical: If the `@decoded` modifier is used in a `param` clause, the referenced parameter on the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be of the bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal charstring type.
requirements.original: In this case, the referenced parameter on the right hand sided of the assignment shall be one of the bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal `charstring types.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the @decoded modifier is used
requirements.canonical: A parameter assigned with the `@decoded` modifier SHALL be decoded into a value of the same type as the variable on the left hand side of the assignment.
requirements.original: It shall be` decoded into a value of the same type as the variable on the left hand side of the assignment.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: decoding fails
requirements.canonical: Failure of the decoding of a parameter assigned with the `@decoded` modifier SHALL cause a test case error.
requirements.original: Failure of this decoding shall cause a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the referenced parameter is of the universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: If the referenced parameter is of the universal charstring type, the `@decoded` clause MAY contain an optional parameter defining the encoding format.
requirements.original: In case the referenced field is of the universal `charstring type, the @decoded` clause can contain an optional parameter defining the encoding format.

ambiguity.issue: The text speaks of a 'referenced field', but in a getcall param clause the referenced item is a signature parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL be of the charstring type.
requirements.original: The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL contain one of the strings allowed for the `decvalue_unichar` function.
requirements.original: The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.canonical: An encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause that is not one of the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Any other value shall cause an error.

ambiguity.issue: The kind of error is not stated; the most likely reading is a test case error at runtime (the value may be non-constant), but a compile-time error is required when the value is known statically.
readings: An encoding format parameter value not allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause a test case error at runtime.
An encoding format parameter value not allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause a compile-time error if it can be determined statically.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-format-parameter
requirements.condition: the referenced parameter is not of the universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: If the referenced parameter is not of the universal charstring type, the encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL NOT be present.
requirements.original: In case the referenced field is not a universal **charstring, the optional** parameter shall not be present.

ambiguity.issue: The text speaks of a 'referenced field', but in a getcall param clause the referenced item is a signature parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.canonical: The `sender` keyword IS used to retrieve the address of the sender of a call accepted by a `getcall` operation, e.g. for addressing a reply or exception to the calling party in a one-to-many configuration.
requirements.original: The keyword sender is used when it is required to retrieve the address of the sender (e.g. for addressing a reply or exception to the calling party in a one-to-many configuration).

requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.condition: no signature argument list is given
requirements.canonical: A `getcall` operation without an argument list for the signature matching criteria removes the call on the top of the incoming port queue (if any) if all other matching criteria are fulfilled.
requirements.original: A getcall operation with no argument list for the signature matching criteria will remove the call on the top of the incoming port queue (if any) if all other matching criteria are fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:any-port
requirements.canonical: A `getcall` on any port IS denoted by the `any` keyword (`any port.getcall`).
requirements.original: To getcall on any port is denoted by the any keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from
requirements.canonical: A `getcall` on any port from a specific port array IS denoted by the `any from` PortArrayRef syntax.
requirements.original: To getcall on any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:port-array-ref
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef in an `any from` `getcall` operation SHALL be a reference to a port array identifier.
requirements.original: To getcall on any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: single-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: For a single-dimensional port array, the index of the port at which the `getcall` operation was successful MAY be stored in a variable of type integer.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a singledimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: For a multi-dimensional port array, the index of the port at which the `getcall` operation was successful MAY be stored in an integer array or record of integer variable.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a singledimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from
requirements.canonical: When an `any from` `getcall` operation checks the port array for matching calls, the iteration over the port indices IS from lowest to highest index.
requirements.original: When checking the port array for matching calls, the port indices to be checked are iterated from lowest to highest.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from
requirements.condition: multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: For a multi-dimensional port array, the ports checked by an `any from` `getcall` operation are iterated from innermost to outermost array dimension, from lowest to highest index for each dimension (e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1]).
requirements.original: If the port array is multi-dimensional, then the ports are iterated over from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].

requirements.subject: ent:any-from
requirements.canonical: The first port of the port array that matches all criteria causes the `any from` `getcall` operation to be successful, even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.
requirements.original: The first port which matches all the criteria will cause the operation to be successful even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.

requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getcall` operation SHALL only be used on procedure-based ports.
requirements.original: a) The getcall operation shall only be used on procedure-based ports.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: The type definition of the port used in a `getcall` operation SHALL include the signature to which the `getcall` operation belongs in its `in` or `inout` list.
requirements.original: The type definition of the port shall include the name of the procedure to which the getcall operation belongs in its in or inout list.

ambiguity.issue: 'procedure' is used where the signature (procedure signature) is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The signature argument of the `getcall` operation SHALL NOT be used to pass in variable names for `in` and `inout` parameters.
requirements.original: b) The signature argument of the getcall operation shall not be used to pass in variable names for in and inout parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:parameter-identifier
requirements.canonical: The ParameterIdentifiers in the `param` clause of a `getcall` operation SHALL be from the corresponding signature definition.
requirements.original: c) The ParameterIdentifiers shall be from the corresponding signature definition.

requirements.subject: ent:value-assignment-part
requirements.canonical: The value assignment part (`-> value`) SHALL NOT be used with the `getcall` operation.
requirements.original: d) The value assignment part shall not be used with the getcall operation.

ambiguity.issue: 'value assignment part' is not defined for getcall; the syntax permits '@index value', so it is unclear what is forbidden. Chosen reading: the value redirect '-> value' known from receive operations.
readings: A value redirect (`-> value VariableRef`) SHALL NOT be used with the `getcall` operation.
No assignment using the `value` keyword (including `@index value`) SHALL be used with the `getcall` operation.

requirements.subject: ent:param-clause
requirements.condition: the getcall operation accepts any call
requirements.canonical: A `getcall` operation without a signature argument (accepting any call) SHALL NOT contain a `param` clause.
requirements.original: e) Parameters of calls accepted by accepting any call shall not be assigned to a variable, i.e. the param clause shall not be present.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: Every AddressRef item in the `from` clause of a `getcall` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `getcall` operation.
requirements.original: f) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the getcall operation.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.canonical: Every ValueRef item in the `sender` clause of a `getcall` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `getcall` operation.
requirements.original: f) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the getcall operation.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: An AddressRef in the `from` clause of a `getcall` operation SHALL NOT contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
requirements.original: No AddressRef in the from clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.

requirements.subject: ent:port-array-ref
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef of a `getcall` operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized port array.
requirements.original: g) The PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: The index redirection (`@index value`) SHALL only be used when the `getcall` operation is used on an `any from` port array construct.
requirements.original: h) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from port array construct.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: single-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a single-dimensional port array, the type of the integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index of the port array.
requirements.original: i) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional port arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the size of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL be exactly the same as the dimension of the port array.
requirements.original: j) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional port arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the element type of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.
requirements.original: j) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional port arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-or-fuzzy-variable
requirements.condition: the redirect variable is a lazy or fuzzy variable
requirements.canonical: If a variable referenced in the `param`, `sender` or `@index` clause of a `getcall` operation is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to that variable IS equal to the result produced by the `getcall` operation.
requirements.original: k) If a variable referenced in the param, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the getcall operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the getcall operation.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-or-fuzzy-variable
requirements.condition: the redirect variable is a lazy or fuzzy variable
requirements.canonical: Later evaluation of a lazy or fuzzy variable referenced in the `param`, `sender` or `@index` clause of a `getcall` operation does NOT lead to repeated invocation of the `getcall` operation.
requirements.original: k) If a variable referenced in the param, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the getcall operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the getcall operation.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.condition: both from and sender clause are present
requirements.canonical: If the `getcall` operation contains both a `from` and a `sender` clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause SHALL be type compatible with the template in the `from` clause.
requirements.original: l) If the getcall operation contains both from and sender clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause shall be type compatible with the template in the from clause.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.condition: sender clause present, from clause absent
requirements.canonical: If the `getcall` operation contains a `sender` clause but no `from` clause, the sender SHALL be type compatible with the type of the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause.
requirements.original: If the operation contains a sender clause but no from clause, the sender shall be type compatible with the type of the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause.

ambiguity.issue: 'the sender' could denote the statically known address type of the port/connection or the actual runtime sender; NOTE 3 suggests a check where the sender type can be determined.
readings: If no `from` clause is present, the type of the sender, where it can be determined statically, SHALL be type compatible with the type of the `sender` clause variable (compile-time check).
If no `from` clause is present, the actual sender address at runtime SHALL be type compatible with the type of the `sender` clause variable, otherwise an error occurs.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: An error due to a type mismatch CAN occur if the types in the signature matching part of a `getcall` operation are not compatible to the types in the assignment part, or if the `from` clause is missing and the type of the sender can be determined and is not type compatible with the type in the `sender` clause.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.

ambiguity.issue: NOTE 3 uses 'receive part' in the getcall clause, where the signature matching part (TemplateInstance) is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:decmatch
requirements.condition: @decoded used together with decmatch matching for the parameter
requirements.canonical: When assigning a parameter decoded with `@decoded` whose matching template uses MatchDecodedContent (`decmatch`) matching, the type of the template in the `decmatch` matching SHALL be type-compatible to the type of the variable the decoded parameter is stored into.
requirements.original: m) When assigning implicitly decoded parameters (by using the @decoded modifier) in cases where the value or template to be matched uses the MatchDecodedContent (decmatch) matching for the parameter to be stored, the type of the template in the MatchDecodedContent matching shall be type-compatible to the type of the variable the decoded field is stored into.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `getcall` operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: n) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:nodefault-modifier
requirements.canonical: The `@nodefault` modifier SHALL only be used in stand-alone `getcall` statements.
requirements.original: o) The @nodefault modifier is allowed only in stand-alone getcall statements.

non_requirement.reason: inline paragraph heading 'Getcall on any port'
inline paragraph heading 'Getcall on any port from a port array'
introduces the restriction list and refers to general static rules in clause 5 and table 16
